answer: A durable defense is earned capacity, not purchased accounts: every new identity starts on low-value jobs and must complete verifiable work before touching larger ones. Each output is independently rerun by two random auditors; a pass raises the identity one ledge at a time, while a failed audit burns its deposit and drops it back to the dune floor. Rewards grow sublinearly with verified output and deposits stay locked per identity, so spawning a thousand fresh accounts costs a thousand deposits and a thousand audited jobs, yet yields no more than one honest agent's meadow of steady work.
